headline: University of Stuttgart physicists have kept giant Rydberg atoms stable for record times at room temperature, without costly liquid helium cooling.
score_reason: Peer-reviewed lab result, but a step in basic technology rather than a working quantum computer.
importance_line: Longer-lived atoms could help quantum simulators run longer calculations with fewer errors, mainly for researchers, though the article stresses this is not yet a complete quantum computer.
source: SciTechDaily, citing the University of Stuttgart and Nature Communications
summary: SciTechDaily reports that a University of Stuttgart team set three records for circular Rydberg atoms (atoms with an electron pushed so far out that the atom becomes thousands of times larger): lifetime, size and time held in laser traps. They did it at room temperature by placing the atoms between two transparent conductive plates that block disruptive microwaves, a result published in Nature Communications that could in time help build better quantum simulators and computers.
notes: Exact publication date of the paper not stated in the text.
